summary: Four of five dimensions FAIL. Spec completeness fails due to REQ-SYNC-024 having no test coverage, validateWebhookRequiredEnvVars declared in purity boundary without a corresponding requirement, missing concurrency specification for webhook processing, and underspecified REQ-SYNC-021. EARS compliance passes — most requirements use proper EARS format with only minor stylistic deviations in REQ-SYNC-013/015 that do not create ambiguity. Purity boundary fails because validateWebhookToken claims constant-time comparison without verification mechanism, canResolveInflightOperation has underspecified integrity-match semantics, and evaluateSubscriptionSearchResult has compressed property descriptions that omit critical fallback branches. Verification coverage fails because of missing INT-SYNC tests for cancel recovery customer_id NULL, cancel pagination limit, and subscription.renewed event processing, plus the sprint contract uses percentage-based grading instead of binary PASS/FAIL. Traceability fails due to the absence of an explicit REQ-SYNC to INT-SYNC mapping matrix.

evidence.description: All 27 requirements reviewed for EARS pattern compliance. 25 of 27 use proper WHEN/THE SYSTEM SHALL or IF/THE SYSTEM SHALL patterns. REQ-SYNC-013 and REQ-SYNC-015 use ubiquitous pattern without trigger but meaning is unambiguous. Findings are minor stylistic issues, not structural EARS violations.
Pure core (lines 11-39) and effectful shell (lines 41-63) reviewed
Purity boundary map (lines 10-70) reviewed. 27 pure functions and 21 effectful functions classified.
15 PROP-SYNC tests, 30 INT-SYNC tests, and 5 mutation testing targets reviewed (lines 76-159)

No REQ-to-INT traceability matrix exists. INT-SYNC numbering does not align with REQ-SYNC numbering (e.g., INT-SYNC-024 covers REQ-SYNC-023, not REQ-SYNC-024). Manual cross-referencing required to verify coverage.
